## Scope and meaning

This extension emits deterministic review candidates from explicit predicates. It does not infer
architectural compliance, disclaimer validity, real-world enforcement, security efficacy or every
possible drift. Source quotations retain their exact text; matching uses the stated normalization.
`SOURCED` applies to the two directly stated v2 radius contracts. The half-to-even clause is
`IMPOSED`, as are Boundary F classification, baseline entries and conservative structural guards.
No current predicate uses `RECOVERED`; no heuristic or similarity matching is presented as recovery.

The full-meaning source survey at the end includes every prose/table unit in the original scope
(BOUNDARIES, NON_GOALS, VERSION_POLICY, GOVERNANCE including §5, SECURITY and all 20 spec docs),
plus the explicit parl packaging deferral. Explanatory statements are retained as well as principles;
that count is not semantic test coverage. Named executable rules check only stated syntactic subsets.

## Verified Boundary F contract (no core/substrate file map)

Scope is root `*.md`, `spec/**/*.md` (including direct children), and comments/docstrings in
`rpp/**/*.py` (including direct children). Everything else is `checkable: no` for Boundary F.
A passage is one Markdown paragraph, list item, table row or complete code fence; or one actual
Python COMMENT token or module/class/function docstring. Headings and table separators are not
passages. Arbitrary executable Python string values are not comments/docstrings. Adjacent list
items and table rows never share a qualifier. A code fence is one block, as TR specified.

Terms are tested against the normalized passage. Only these physics terms count:
spintronic, spin state, decoher*, T2, t2_ns, thermaliz*, thermodynam*, Hamiltonian, physics,
physically, physical invariant, material property, hologra*, wave interference. Case is ignored
except exact `T2` and `t2_ns`; those literals also match identifier fragments such as min_t2_ns.
Bare coherence, resonance, substrate, hardware, physical and quantum do not establish a physics match.

Normative: case-sensitive `\b(MUST|SHALL|REQUIRED)( NOT)?\b`, or the exact lowercase phrases
“not a valid”, “must be rejected”, “refuse”, and uppercase “ABORT”. There is no repository RFC 2119.
Lowercase “must” alone is `checkable: no` as a normative claim; it never creates a HIGH classification.
Qualifiers are case-insensitive “On spintronic(s)”, “on spintronic hardware/platforms/substrates”,
or “(spintronic)”. No semantic interpretation extends this list.

- **BND-F-1 HIGH:** new/changed passage with physics + normative and no qualifier; independently,
  disappearance of any normalized software-MUST anchor below is HIGH.
- **BND-F-2 MEDIUM, report only:** any other new/changed physics-term passage.
- **BND-F-BASELINE-REMOVED MEDIUM, report only:** known baseline passage removed or rewritten
  without physics terms. Name its id, file, old line hint and old normalized hash. Q1 explicitly
  requires a finding; absence does not close or accept an entry. A physical rewrite is classified
  normally by F-1/F-2; its prior id/hash remains in the separate baseline change event.
- Disclaimers (“advisory”, “not a claim”, “must not assert”), quantum vocabulary, software
  “equivalence” and coherence-as-scalar are `checkable: no` as semantic defenses or claims.
  They do not create an inferred exemption from the explicit predicates.

The premise that hardware enforcement is optional and software MUSTs govern is **IMPOSED**:
for it, SPEC.md:56, SPINTRONIC.md:19 and PRIMER.md:276; against it, DEPLOYABLE.md:17–18
and SPINTRONIC.md:207. This inventory retains that tension rather than resolving it.

Exact implementation regexes:

- `physics`: `(?i:\bspintronics?\b|\bspin state\b|\bdecoher\w*|\bthermaliz\w*|\bthermodynam\w*|\bHamiltonian\b|\bphysics\b|\bphysically\b|\bphysical invariant\b|\bmaterial property\b|\bhologra\w*|\bwave interference\b)|(?<![A-Za-z0-9])(?:T2|t2_ns)(?![A-Za-z0-9])`

- `normative`: `\b(?:MUST|SHALL|REQUIRED)(?: NOT)?\b|\bnot a valid\b|\bmust be rejected\b|\brefuse\b|\bABORT\b`

- `qualifier`: `\bon spintronics?(?:\s+(?:hardware|platforms|substrates))?\b|\(spintronic\)`

## Identity, movement, reporting and exits

Hash Git **blob** text, not a CRLF worktree: normalize line endings to LF, normalize Unicode to
NFC, collapse each whitespace run to one ASCII space, trim, then SHA-256 over UTF-8. Quotes,
comment delimiters and fence delimiters belong to their passage text. Case is preserved.
Match passages by hash, preferring same-path occurrences before cross-file moves. The line is a
hint, not identity. Equal-hash moves/rewrapping do not create drift findings; moves are reported in
`baseline_events` separately from changed/removed text. Duplicates are matched by occurrence count.
Different hashes are never matched by similarity. Replacement uses an exact bipartite graph of
atomic Git edit runs (split at unchanged context) and unchanged LF-line coordinate mappings.
ALL parsed old/new units participate, including nonphysics units. A physical replacement requires
one old and one new passage in the component with the same path, kind, and structural owner.
The owner is the Markdown heading hierarchy or Python enclosing class/function names; it is not
inferred from meaning. Another physics passage in the same hunk can never supply replacement scope.

**IMPOSED conservative choices (CX-004 A2):** split/merge or multi-unit components, changed-text
renames, changed owners and kind changes retain the removal finding and independently classify
new physics wording. Exact-hash moves remain exempt, including cross-file renames; equal-hash
rewrapping/end-line/owner changes are reported as moved even when the start line is unchanged.

Every baseline entry remains IMPOSED, **unresolved - steward decision (RADIX)**, routed `[RFC]`
via TR under GOVERNANCE.md:63–71. DECISIONS.md is absent at the source revision. Every run prints
the full open-baseline count, even if entries are absent from the target; no entry is marked accepted.

The four separate MEDIUM steward items below are not Boundary F rules. On every run, show their
open count in `summary.open_steward_items` and list unchanged items under “Open steward items
(unchanged)”. Unchanged items do **not** affect exit status (TR Q2). A changed cited passage is a
normal finding at its own severity. The two unchanged LOW advisory groups are displayed separately.

Canonical Git diff flags ignore color/prefix/algorithm/function-caption settings and force text
only after BOTH sides of every reviewed source path have passed regular-file, UTF-8/NUL and size
validation. A binary attribute cannot suppress a text predicate. Git lines are split on LF only,
not Unicode line separators. These requirements also apply to WORD-only Markdown paths.

Exit 0 means no HIGH/MEDIUM **diff findings**; 1 means HIGH/MEDIUM diff findings; 2 means tool error
or incomplete review. CI remains advisory for all outcomes. Findings sort HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, then
rule id, path and integer line; evidence/source break ties. Addition lines belong to head, deletion
lines to base, mode-only events use 0. `rules_run` counts configured executable rules evaluated;
`rules_not_checkable` counts full-meaning source-survey units, not defects.

Only hexadecimal commit ids are accepted. Evaluation reads Git objects, never target imports,
checkouts or target tests. Renames are deletion/addition, with equal-hash Boundary F moves paired
across the scanned paths. Reviewed source limit is 4 MiB, reviewed diff limit 16 MiB. Malformed
UTF-8, unreadable/nonregular review blobs or unparsable scoped Python cause tool error. Other
content predicates keep their documented scopes; only Boundary F uses this all-passage scope.

## Radius amendments

Scope: **Ra-Canonical v2 only**, bits [20:13], `RPPAddress.radius`. GEOMETRY.md:52's minor radius
and Mobius32 are excluded; parl/ is not packaged in the root wheel (pyproject.toml:57),
`checkable: no`. The API is float 0.0–1.0 (SOURCED: RPP-CANONICAL-v2.md:219,229,362;
rpp/address_canonical.py:253). The HDL port carries the byte (RPP-CANONICAL-v2.md:292).
The encoded contract is `round(radius*255) & 0xFF`, byte 0–255 (SOURCED:
RPP-CANONICAL-v2.md:168–170,239; rpp/address_canonical.py:308).
The separate **IMPOSED** half-to-even clause follows Python round; fixed vectors:
`1/510 -> 0`, `5/510 -> 2`, `0.5 -> 128`. Quantization-call AST changes are review candidates.

LOW wording sites are VERSION_POLICY.md:83,70,74; spec/README.md:92;
spec/PMA-SCHEMA-v1.md:116; spec/ADDRESSING-LAYERS.md:114. Static advisories are shown without
editing those sources. A source edit yields the LOW wording diff finding.
The True/-0.0 guard and negative-zero URI mismatch are a separate LOW item, not a silent source fix.

Non-F text-boundary scope: the explicit `boundary_text_paths` and `core_globs` in catalog.json
(retained initial syntactic subsets, not a claim of a repository core/substrate map). Address AST
scope: rpp/address.py, rpp/address_canonical.py and reference/python/rpp_address.py. Frozen format
projection watches uppercase field/address constants and encode/decode/to_int/to_raw/from_int/
from_raw/__post_init__/is_valid functions; comments/docstrings and AST coordinates are ignored.
VER-FORMAT-1 is suppressed only by an increased `**RPP Specification Version:**` MAJOR in
VERSION_POLICY.md. Radius, boundary and vector findings are not suppressed by that bump.
The two radius contract projections apply only within rpp/address_canonical.py and the cited v2
source guards. Source-guard comparisons are normalized; raw diff excerpts remain the evidence.

Vector globs: tests/*golden* and tests/*vector* (fnmatch includes subdirectories). Unconventionally
named future vectors need an explicit catalog update. Any modification/addition/deletion/mode
change is HIGH, requiring RADIX; no fixture edits a real golden vector. WORD-CLAIM-1 checks added
Markdown outside tools/drift/, whose source inventory and evidence quote claims rather than making
them. That check is a wording candidate only; it cannot determine whether a shown basis is adequate.

| P-1324 | **1. No edges, no corners.** A flat address space (IPv4's 0 to 2^32) has a beginning and<br>an end. The address 0.0.0.0 and 255.255.255.255 are qualitatively different from<br>192.168.1.1. Corner addresses require special handling. A torus has no corners. Every<br>point on a torus has the same local neighborhood — the same number of adjacent addresses,<br>reachable by the same angular arithmetic. These two properties<br>are genuinely orthogonal — changing the consent level of a record does not change what kind<br>of data it is. The torus encodes this orthogonality structurally. | P-2049 | Software timeouts are promises. A Shell=0 TTL of 25 nanoseconds implemented purely in software is a statement of intent: the runtime *should* expire the key after 25 ns. Whether it actually does depends on the scheduler, the thread priority, OS interrupt latency, and the trustworthiness of the implementation. A sufficiently privileged process can read memory before the software deadline fires. A cold-boot attack captures DRAM state after power loss. A cache-timing side channel can extract key material from L1 cache long after the nominal TTL has expired. | spec/SPINTRONIC.md:13 | MEDIUM | no | IMPOSED | This statement requires semantic/operational interpretation, a quantified execution model, or external evidence; no approved diff predicate asserts its full meaning. Numeric examples and reference code are not universal validation. |
| P-2050 | Physical enforcement is different in kind, not in degree. When the enforcing mechanism is a property of matter — the spin coherence time of electrons in a solid-state lattice — there is no software path that bypasses it. You cannot patch the Hamiltonian. You cannot &#96;sudo&#96; your way around T2 decoherence. The key state is not hidden; it is gone. | spec/SPINTRONIC.md:15 | MEDIUM | no | IMPOSED | This statement requires semantic/operational interpretation, a quantified execution model, or external evidence; no approved diff predicate asserts its full meaning. Numeric examples and reference code are not universal validation. |

| P-2054 | Electrons carry intrinsic angular momentum — spin — which is a two-state quantum system: spin-up ($&#124;\uparrow\rangle$) or spin-down ($&#124;\downarrow\rangle$), or any quantum superposition thereof. In a spintronic device, information is encoded in the spin state of one or more electrons rather than (or in addition to) their charge. The spin state of a qubit-like register can be initialized, rotated, and read out using magnetic fields, spin-transfer torque, or optical pumping, depending on the substrate. | spec/SPINTRONIC.md:29 | MEDIUM | no | IMPOSED | This statement requires semantic/operational interpretation, a quantified execution model, or external evidence; no approved diff predicate asserts its full meaning. | P-2055 | Spin coherence is the property that makes spin states useful for information storage: a spin that is initialized to a known state will remain in that state — remain *coherent* — for some finite duration before random perturbations (thermal fluctuations, lattice vibrations, magnetic noise from nearby nuclei, spin-orbit coupling) scramble it into an incoherent mixture. After decoherence, the spin state carries no recoverable information about its initial value. | spec/SPINTRONIC.md:31 | MEDIUM | no | IMPOSED | This statement requires semantic/operational interpretation, a quantified execution model, or external evidence; no approved diff predicate asserts its full meaning. T1 is typically longer than T2. | spec/SPINTRONIC.md:35 | MEDIUM | no | IMPOSED | This statement requires semantic/operational interpretation, a quantified execution model, or external evidence; no approved diff predicate asserts its full meaning. | P-2058 | - **T2 (spin-spin dephasing time, or transverse relaxation time):** The time for phase coherence to be lost due to random fluctuations in the local magnetic environment.
